title: Current Electricity
seo_title: Current Electricity Class 12 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 3)
standard_text: Electric current, flow of electric charges in a metallic conductor, drift velocity, mobility and their relation with electric current; Ohm's law, V–I characteristics (linear and non-linear), electrical energy and power, electrical resistivity and conductivity, temperature dependence of resistance, internal resistance of a cell, potential difference and emf of a cell, combination of cells in series and in parallel, Kirchhoff's rules, Wheatstone bridge.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 3 Current Electricity: current and drift velocity, Ohm's law, resistivity, resistors in series and parallel, power, cells, Kirchhoff's rules and the Wheatstone bridge. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Kirchhoff: current in = current out; ΣV round a loop = 0.
body_html:
How to think about it

Current I = Q/t = neAvd, where the drift velocity is only about a millimetre per second. Ohm's law V = IR holds for ohmic conductors; resistance R = ρl/A rises with temperature for metals. Resistors add in series and their reciprocals add in parallel; power is VI = I²R = V²/R.

A cell of e.m.f. E and internal resistance r gives I = E/(R + r). Kirchhoff's junction rule (charge) and loop rule (energy) solve networks; a Wheatstone bridge balances when P/Q = R/S.

Example

P = 10, Q = 20, R = 15. S?

RQ/P

Answer: 30 Ω

Example

E = 12 V, r = 1 Ω, R = 5 Ω. I?

12 ÷ 6

Answer: 2 A

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting internal resistance.
  • Thinking electrons move at light speed.
  • Adding parallel resistances directly.

faq.q: Why is drift velocity so small but a bulb lights at once?
faq.a: The electric field travels along the wire almost instantly, so all the free electrons start drifting together.

faq.q: What is a balanced Wheatstone bridge?
faq.a: When P/Q = R/S no current flows through the galvanometer.
